name: Morphology (ṣarf)
definition: The science of the forms of single words: how one root takes different patterns, and what changes inside a word apart from its ending.
body: Ṣarf, also called taṣrīf, looks at a word on its own. It studies the patterns (awzān) that root letters are poured into, how a verb is conjugated through persons and tenses, and how nouns such as the doer and the one acted on are derived from one root.

In the madrasa, ṣarf is usually read first, because naḥw speaks of the endings of words whose forms the student must already recognise. A saying the teachers repeat calls ṣarf the mother of the sciences and naḥw their father.

examples.text: From one root, n-ṣ-r: he helped, he helps, a helper, helped.
